attack_chain.action: Malware captures the output of the executed command, encodes it with base64, and sends it back to the C2 server via HTTP POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives command output and can continue interactive control (reverse shell).

behavioral_signatures: Outbound HTTPS requests to pypi.python.org with non-standard Host headers (e.g., psec.forward.io.global.prod.fastly.net)
Base64-encoded data in query strings to /images or similar endpoints on pypi.python.org
Execution of shell commands based on remote HTTP responses using subprocess.Popen with shell=True
HTTP POST requests containing base64-encoded command output to Fastly CDN endpoints
file_indicators: Presence of code manipulating Host headers in Python requests
References to psec.forward.io.global.prod.fastly.net or similar Fastly subdomains in source code
Code invoking subprocess.Popen with shell=True and handling remote command input
network_indicators: HTTPS requests to pypi.python.org with Host header set to psec.forward.io.global.prod.fastly.net
Outbound traffic to Fastly CDN endpoints not matching normal PyPI usage patterns
HTTP POST requests with base64-encoded payloads to /images or similar paths
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python processes making HTTPS requests to pypi.python.org with suspicious Host headers (such as psec.forward.io.global.prod.fastly.net). Flag base64-encoded data in query strings to /images endpoints. Detect subprocess or shell command execution triggered by remote HTTP responses, especially via subprocess.Popen with shell=True. Correlate with unusual outbound traffic patterns to CDN infrastructure and look for references to Fastly subdomains in source code.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At import-time, the code collects the username, hostname, and current working directory, then sends this data as HTTP GET parameters to an attacker-controlled server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive host information to an external server via an HTTP GET request, which is a direct and observable method of data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not send system information to external servers during import or installation, especially not to hardcoded, untrusted domains and without user awareness.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Error reporting or telemetry may send limited data to trusted domains, but only with user consent and never with sensitive host details as GET parameters.
key_indicators: Sensitive host information sent as HTTP GET parameters
Hardcoded attacker-controlled URL (security.hsd1.co)
Network exfiltration at import-time
No user notification or opt-in

package_info.why_malicious: The package is malicious because it covertly collects sensitive host information (such as username, hostname, and current working directory) at import-time and exfiltrates this data to attacker-controlled infrastructure using both DNS queries with encoded subdomains and HTTP requests. This enables stealthy data theft without user knowledge or consent.

attack_chain.leads_to: Data is prepared for exfiltration.

Base64 encoding of system information for network transmission
DNS queries to suspicious or attacker-controlled domains with encoded subdomains
HTTP requests to hardcoded, non-standard domains containing host/user info in parameters or URL path
Network exfiltration logic present in __init__.py or main.py

References to external domains such as dns1.thewhybee.com, security.hsd1.co, enjglpdgtgrbn4b.m.pipedream.net
Presence of Base64 encoding and network modules (socket, requests) in top-level package files
network_indicators: DNS queries to *.dns1.thewhybee.com with long, encoded subdomains
HTTP GET requests to http://security.hsd1.co/6ca3/ with host/user info as parameters

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that, during installation or import, collect system information (username, hostname, working directory) and transmit it via DNS queries with encoded subdomains or HTTP requests to untrusted domains. Flag packages that reference known attacker infrastructure, perform network operations without user consent, or contain suspicious code in __init__.py or main.py that leverages Base64 encoding and network modules for exfiltration.
